result.title: AT-AT: Automatic Tool Optimization from Agent Traces
result.summary: Efforts to improve LLM-based agents typically focus on modifying the agent itself, yet success also depends on the environment in which an agent acts. Tools mediate this interaction: a tool's description shapes how an agent calls it, and its implementation determines the results and errors the agent receives afterwards. Many tools, such as APIs and MCP servers, are shared by many agents and maintained by providers who cannot change those agents. We introduce AT-AT (Automatic Tool Optimization from Agent Traces), an agentic tool optimizer that improves a shared toolset offline from historical agent executions while holding the agents fixed. A lightweight coding agent reads agent trajectories and their evaluation results, and selectively edits tool descriptions and, when permitted, implementations. On $τ^2$-bench-verified, AT-AT achieves the highest task completion rates in the Airline and Telecom domains at lower cost than strong prompt- and tool-optimizer baselines, and its Telecom gain is statistically significant under paired permutation tests. Optimizing the tools within a coding agent harness also improves held-out performance on TerminalBench-2 and TBLite. When applied to three production MCP servers at a large enterprise, AT-AT lowered cost or tool error rates on every server and increased held-out task passes on one. By turning accumulated execution traces into updates to shared tool environments, AT-AT provides a path toward continual improvement of agent systems through environment-side learning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AT-AT：在保持 agent 固定的前提下，用一个轻量 coding agent 读取历史执行轨迹及评估结果，离线选择性地改写共享工具的描述（在允许时也修改实现），并在 τ²-bench 与企业 MCP 服务器上考察任务完成率、成本和工具错误率。
AI.relevance_reason: 把轨迹中的失败归因到「证据获取接口」并据此改进环境侧，可能为 LVR 的工具/视觉证据通道设计与轨迹级贡献分配提供借鉴线索，但该文不涉及 latent 状态或多模态推理本身，迁移价值需核查。
